question.problem:
The table below gives the medication infusion rate $r(t)$, in milligrams per minute, for a patient.

| $t\,\text{(minutes)}$ | $0$ | $4$ | $7$ | $10$ | $13$ | $18$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $r(t)\,\text{(mg/min)}$ | $6$ | $5$ | $3$ | $4$ | $2$ | $1$ |

Use the right Riemann sum over $[0,18]$ with five subintervals to approximate the total medication delivered (in milligrams).

The total medication delivered is
{{field-1}} milligrams.
question.worked_solution:
Let $A$ denote the area under the curve $y=r(t)$ over $[0,18].$ In this case, we have $n=5$ rectangles. Using the right Riemann sum, the area is computed as 

$$
A≈r(4)Δ{t}_{1}+r(7)Δ{t}_{2}+r(10)Δ{t}_{3}+r(13)Δ{t}_{4}+r(18)Δ{t}_{5},
$$

where each $Δ{t}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $t$-value and the previous one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{t}_{i}={t}_{i}-{t}_{i-1}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δt$'s.

| $t$ | $0$ | $4$ | $7$ | $10$ | $13$ | $18$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δt$ | $-$ | $4$ | $3$ | $3$ | $3$ | $5$ |
| $r(t)$ | $-$ | $5$ | $3$ | $4$ | $2$ | $1$ |

We plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈5\cdot 4+3\cdot 3+4\cdot 3+2\cdot 3+1\cdot 5 \\  & =20+9+12+6+5 \\  & =52.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total accumulation of medication. So, the total medication delivered is $52$ milligrams.
